model.architecture: A 1.54B code model at **1.12 GB** — small enough that a phone-class device runs it at conversational speed rather than merely running it.

variants.quantization: int4 blockwise-32 + OCTAV on linears, int8 embedding (externalised)

recommended.reason: measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 8.55 tok/s decode / 234.9 prefill, peak 885 MB, init 8.3 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-24, 1 run) against CPU 27.01-29.73 decode / 57.1-106.0 prefill, peak 1566 MB, init 2.7 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken: the CPU decodes 3.3x faster than the GPU on this handset, so the earlier GPU choice is reversed; gpu keeps the prefill advantage for prompt-heavy, short-output work

platform_notes: A Mac's GPU-vs-CPU ratio (GPU decodes 2.9x CPU here) does not transfer to a phone; on phone hardware the GPU's win is prefill and time-to-first-token.
Embedding table is stored in its own bundle section, keeping the file at 1.12 GB (inline it would be 2.53 GB).
Android GPU: XNNPACK takes 1 of 4 nodes in decode_embedder and prefill_embedder_1024; the runtime accepts that split.
4096-token KV budget and six prefill signatures (1024, 256, 64, 16, 4, 1).
Chat template bakes in Qwen's default system prompt, inserted when no system message is supplied.

measured.source: model card: Raspberry Pi 5 (CPU) table (card retrieved 2026-09-05)

S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (8451 ops across 7 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart
